body.statement: In the specialization \(N=3,r=s=1\) and \(\gamma=\kappa_\star=1/\sqrt3\), the maximal-margin loading class is exactly \(\{\operatorname{range}(P_h):h\in\mathcal H_4\}\). Distinct projectors satisfy \(\lVert P_h-P_{h'}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=2\sqrt2/3\). For the four-hypothesis Gaussian experiment \(\mathcal E_4(T_0)\), with nuisance parameters \(d,f,\sigma\) profiled over their full stated sets, the nearest-projector rule obeys \(\max_{h\in\mathcal H_4}\sup_{d,f,\sigma}\mathbb P_{h,d,f,\sigma}(\widehat h\ne h)\le p_{\mathrm{cls}}(T_0)=\min\{1,18V_0/(T_0d_{\mathrm{lo}}^4)\}\). Hence \(T_0\ge\overline T\) implies uniform misclassification probability at most \(\alpha/2\).
body.justification: The explicit profiled experiment turns the endpoint geometry into a uniform finite-sample decision bound with a declared error budget.
body.gap: EvansHansenStark2005 supplies abstract confidence-set decision duality but does not identify these four Gaussian components or profile the panel nuisances \(d,f,\sigma\).
body.consumer: It certifies when a loading-margin oracle may spend part of its noncoverage budget on component classification without widening the reported effect set.
